artboards.title: As it stands today, with its faults marked
Proposed -- the Map console, a place selected
Proposed -- the Deliveries layer, today's round
Proposed -- brand new, offline, settled, and empty

annotations.text:
WHAT I ASKED, AND WHAT YOU SAID

1. The job. All four -- who owes me where, what is going
out today, where is this customer, and putting places on
the map. So the screen cannot pick one; it has to stop
making you choose between them.

2. Pinning. "Should be automatic." Suggest, and I confirm
each one.

3. Where. Desktop at the desk. The phone gets a real but
smaller design, not the desk reflowed.

4. Deliveries. Stays here, as a layer.

WHAT THE PAGE IS ACTUALLY ABOUT

Not the map. The map is how PLACES are drawn. Once you
say that, the screen falls out: places are the object,
the map is one view of them, the list is the other, and
"not placed yet" stops being a separate mode and becomes
one row in the list that happens to be missing a
position.

Everything on the right is built on that.

NINE THINGS WRONG WITH IT TODAY >

They are marked on the board to the right, in order.

1. Layer (Customers / Suppliers / Deliveries) and filter
   (All / To place / On the map) are different kinds of
   control drawn as the same pill, 300px apart. One
   changes what the screen is about; the other changes
   which rows are listed.
2. The only figures on the page are a 12.5px grey
   sentence squeezed beside a search box. There is no
   metric strip. The screen's own answer is its smallest
   text.
3. The legend paints "Under 30 days" and "Nothing owed"
   the same #1C6B58. Two entries, one colour: a key that
   lies about the thing it is a key to.
4. The compass is built from glyphs -- the system says
   draw the mark, never borrow one.
5. A 300px rail holds one sentence until you click
   something. A quarter of the console, idle, on open.
6. The amber strip says "find them in the list below and
   press Place" -- it names the work instead of offering
   it.
7. Far places are chips. A chip cannot carry the 530,000
   owed out there, so the figure is simply not shown.
8. Unplaced sorts first by design, so the busiest place
   in the shop is last in the list.
9. No figure is monospaced or right-aligned -- against
   the system's own rule that money is a component. And
   the list dot is placed/unplaced only; it never carries
   the aging band the markers are coloured by.

Also, and not visible: #mp_search is used twice in
index.html -- the map's search box and the media picker's
-- so getElementById can bind renderMapResults to the
wrong input. That is a bug, not a design note.

THE PROPOSAL -- what changed, and why

THE ANSWER BEFORE THE PICTURE. You chose a metric strip, and it earns the place: four figures, one 64px band, hairline dividers, no
per-tile borders. Owed to you; oldest debt; most owed in one place; not on the map yet. The third is the one the old page could never
say -- Bwaise is 36% of everything you are owed, and that is the sentence a collection round is planned from.

ONE ACCENT, ON THE ONE THING TO DO NEXT. "Place 6 remaining", in the header. Nothing else on the screen is oxide. When every place is
placed, the button is not there at all and the screen has no accent -- which is correct, because then there is nothing to do next.

LAYER AND FILTER STOP LOOKING ALIKE. The layer switch becomes one segmented control in the panel head, with counts on it, sitting on
the thing it governs. The list filter is the same object down in the list, where it governs the list. Same component, two places, each
attached to what it changes -- instead of two pill rows that mean different things and look identical.

THE RAIL ANSWERS BEFORE YOU CLICK. Click a marker and it is the place. But it does not open empty: the panel is the selected place,
with what is owed, what you owe, the oldest debt, and every customer there as a row with a figure -- so the rail is the same width it
always was and finally worth it.

THE LEGEND COMES OFF THE MAP. It was covering the map's bottom-left corner, and "nothing owed" is now a hollow ring rather than a
second green. It sits under the map as one row, and carries the two things a reader cannot deduce: circle size is headcount, the
square is your shop.

FAR PLACES BECOME A LIST, NOT CHIPS. Jinja, 81km, 410,000 owed, 44 days. A chip could carry the first two.

ONE LIST, TWO JOBS. Finding a place you have and placing one you have not are the same row. An unplaced place keeps its figures, keeps
its rank -- Nansana is fourth by money owed, so it is fourth in the list -- and carries a dashed ring and one action instead of being
exiled to a strip. There is no second mode.

MONEY IS A COMPONENT. Every figure is IBM Plex Mono, tabular, right-aligned, unit under it. The name column gives way; the figure never
truncates.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DECIDED FOR YOU

1. THE AUTOMATIC PIN NEEDS A LOOKUP SERVICE.
   You said suggest-and-confirm. That means the app has
   to ask something where "Nansana" is -- Nominatim, on
   OpenStreetMap's data, is free and needs no key, but
   it is a network call and it has a usage policy. The
   code today deliberately has no geocoder ("there are
   no addresses here to give one"). This is the one
   change in the whole proposal that adds a dependency.
   Worth confirming before I build it.

2. WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE LOOKUP IS WRONG.
   Drawn here as: accept, "not there -- I'll click it",
   or skip. A name that matches nothing says so and
   waits, rather than being placed somewhere plausible.
   I think that is right. Say if you would rather it
   guessed and flagged.

3. "CHASE THESE THREE" IN THE RAIL.
   I put it there because a place with 1,480,000 at 94
   days is a collection round. It goes to Debtors with
   the three pre-selected -- it does NOT send anything.
   If you would rather the map never offered it, it
   comes out and the rail keeps only "Move pin".

4. THE FOURTH STRIP TILE.
   "Most owed in one place" versus something else --
   number of places, say, or this week's collections.
   It is the tile I am least sure of.

5. THE SHOP'S OWN PIN.
   Shown in the header as "The shop is in Kisenyi", and
   as a black square on the map. Today it is inferred
   from the printed shop address. Should it be settable
   here, or stay in Presets?

THE DELIVERY LAYER -- kept, as you asked, but made to change the question

Switching layer changes what the four figures mean, because it changes what you are asking. Going out today; to collect on delivery;
no driver yet; furthest stop. "To collect" is the balance still unpaid, never the order's value -- on a part-paid order those are
different numbers, and the balance is the one the driver is accountable for.

TWO COLOURS, BOTH FROM THE PALETTE. The old page painted assigned stops #2F7FBF -- a blue that is not one of the 23 values and means
nothing in this app. Amber is "no driver yet", which is the thing you can act on before the van leaves; verdigris is "driver
assigned". No fourth state, no invented colour.

WHAT THE MAP CANNOT DRAW IS SAID OUT LOUD. A stop whose place has no pin, an order with no destination on file, and a customer
collecting in person are three different problems, and none of them is "missing". They get their own panel with their own figures.

THE ROUND IS ORDERED NEAREST-FIRST, not most-owed-first, because that is how a driver is briefed. The stops are the same stops Order
tracking shows, from the same working -- so the two can never hold different opinions about today. And nothing here dispatches
anybody: handing an order to a driver is still your tap, on Order tracking.

PLACING, AS A QUESTION -- not as a chore

You said the app should suggest and you confirm each one.
So the screen asks.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. The map dims the pins that are
already set and draws ONE dashed oxide ring where it
thinks Nansana is. Dashed, hollow, and labelled
"suggested" -- it must not be possible to mistake a
proposal for a pin that has been set.

THE PANEL BESIDE IT ASKS THE QUESTION. "Is this
Nansana?", the full name it matched, where the guess came
from, how far from the shop, and what is waiting there --
620,000, 58 days, two customers. Then one accent button.
Accepting moves straight to the next, so six places is
six taps.

THE ACCENT IS HERE, AND ONLY HERE. The header's "Place 6
remaining" turns into a ghost "Stop placing" while this
is running. The row down in the list REPORTS the
suggestion but does not offer a second accept -- two
accepts for one pin is two chances to answer differently.

NOTHING IS WRITTEN UNTIL YOU SAY SO, and the strip's
fourth tile says exactly that while the placing runs.

A NAME THAT MATCHED NOTHING SAYS SO. "Bukoto East, Plot 4
-- no match found. Click the map instead." It is not
dropped from the queue, and it is not placed somewhere
plausible. Named rather than dropped.

THE FOUR STATES, WHICH IS WHERE A SCREEN IS ACTUALLY DESIGNED >

1. BRAND NEW. The old page showed an empty grey rectangle with a legend floating on it. What matters here is that THE FIGURES ARE
ALREADY RIGHT -- they are counted from invoices, not from the map -- so the empty state says so, and then names the work: place them,
and I have suggestions for 19 of the 23. Four matched nothing, and it says that too rather than letting you find out one at a time.

2. NO CONNECTION. The tiles are the only thing on this screen that needed the network. So the screen loses the picture, keeps the
answer, and says which of the two it lost. The rail fills with where the money is, as a list -- because that was the question, and it
can still be answered. A failure must name itself; a grey box is not a failure message.

3. EVERYTHING PLACED, NOBODY OWES ANYTHING. Not an error and not a blank: the good news, said. The map still draws all 23, because
where people are is worth knowing whether or not they owe you. Both zero tiles go verdigris.

4. DELIVERIES, NOTHING WAITING. Names what would put something here -- an order joins the round once it is invoiced AND marked for
delivery rather than collection -- and says six are sitting in exactly that gap.

THE PHONE -- its own design, not the desk reflowed

820px is a switch between two designs. You said the desk
is the real one, so the phone is deliberately smaller in
ambition: the same four answers, then the picture, then
the places as cards.

WHAT CHANGED FROM THE DESK. The strip becomes 2x2 in one
card. The layer switch becomes a full-width segmented
control -- a row of pills is three separate 30px targets
in a yard, in sun. The table becomes cards with the
figure and the meta visible without opening anything.
The map is 170px, which is enough to see WHERE, and the
list is what you read.

THE ACCENT IS IN THE THUMB ZONE. "Place the 6 remaining"
sits just above the tab bar at 48px, not in a header the
thumb cannot reach.

THE TAB BAR IS THE HOUSE FIVE, unchanged -- Today, Sell,
Money, Manager, More -- with More filled, because Map is
reached from there. Active is FILLED and inactive is
stroked; a shape change reads where a colour change
alone does not. I have not proposed making Map a sixth
tab; that is a navigation decision, not a map one.
